summary: Vasily Radlov worked in linguistics, Central Asian studies, and archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Jena under Pott, Steinthal, and Schott. He directed the Asiatic Museum (1885–1890) and the Peter the Great Museum (1894–1918).

Vasily Seseman was a philosopher who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1903–1909). He held academic posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1915–1919), Vytautas Magnus University (~1923–1940), and Vilnius University (~1940–1950).

Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his PhD at the University of Bonn in 1930. He taught at Visva-Bharati University, Fergusson College, and the University of Delhi (appointed professor in 1959).

Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi worked in Indology and history/archaeology, earning degrees from Deccan College and the University of Mumbai. He served as Principal of Morris College and Vidarbha Institute, and was Honorary Professor at Nagpur University from 1957 to 1966.

Vasudeva Sharan Agrawala was an Indologist and historian who earned degrees from Banaras Hindu University and the University of Lucknow. He served as Curator of the Mathura Museum (1931), Director of Lucknow State Museum (1940), and Superintendent at the Archaeological Survey of India (1946).

Vasudha Dalmia is an Indologist and historian who earned degrees from Miranda House, University of Cologne, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Heidelberg University. She held professorships at the University of California, Berkeley (2001–2012) and Yale University (2013–2014).

Vasudha Narayanan is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the Universities of Madras, Mumbai, and Harvard. She was appointed Distinguished Professor of Religion at the University of Florida in ~1982 and served as President of the American Academy of Religion (~2001–2002).

Vasumati Karandikar is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. She earned degrees from the University of Mumbai (M.A. 2017–2019, 2022–2024) and completed her Ph.D. at Kavikulaguru Kalidas Sanskrit University in 2021.

Vatroslav Jagić was a linguist who studied under Miklosich, Leskien, and Weber at the universities of Vienna and Leipzig. He held professorships at Odesa University (1871–1874), Humboldt University of Berlin (1874–1880), Saint Petersburg State University (1880–1886), and Vienna (1886–1909).

Vedprakash Sharma is an Indologist who completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Delhi (1980–1985) and earned a Ph.D. from Maharshi Dayanand University (2005–2008). He has served as a Research Associate at the University of Delhi.

Veeranarayana N. K. Pandurangi works in Indology, philosophy, and computational linguistics. He studied under Manikya Shastri and Martanda Dikshit, earning PhDs from Central and National Sanskrit Universities. He has held posts at French Institute of Pondicherry, Rajasthan Sanskrit University, and Karnataka Samskrit University.

Velcheru Narayana Rao is an Indologist who studied at Sir C. R. Reddy College, Andhra University (M.A., Ph.D.), and Osmania University. He served as a lecturer and Associate Professor of South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1971.

Velizar Sadovski is a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (1996–2001) and has served there as Universitätsdozent (2001) and at the Austrian Academy of Sciences from 1998.

Vempati Kutumba Sastry is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Central Sanskrit University from 2003 to 2008 and was President of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies from ~2006 to 2018.

Ven. Dhammapāla is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bhante Dhammasakkaro and K. L. Dhammajoti. He attended the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong.

Venoth Nallisamy works in Indology. He studied at Universiti Malaysia Sabah, Open University Malaysia, and the University of Malaya, where he completed his PhD. In 2024, he became a Senior Lecturer at INTI International University.

Vera Aleksandrovna Novikova was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov and Aleksandr Semënovič Zimin, later working at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (1949–1950) and teaching Indian philology at Saint Petersburg State University (1952).

Verity Harte is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge (1986–1994). She held research and teaching posts at St Edmund's College, St Hilda's College, Oxford, and King's College London, before becoming Professor of Philosophy and Classics at Yale in 2006.

Verrier Elwin was a scholar in Indology and archaeology who studied at Merton College, Oxford. He served as Deputy-Director of the Anthropological Survey of India (1946–1949) and Adviser for Tribal Affairs for the North-East Frontier Agency in 1954.

Vesna Wallace is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed her doctorate at the University of California, Berkeley. She held the Numata Chair in Buddhist Studies at Oxford (until 2010) and currently serves as Professor at UC Santa Barbara.
